title: Cart drawer total is one cent above the checkout total with the bundle promotion
description: With three units of a 13.99 item and the 10 percent bundle promotion, the cart drawer shows 41.97 while checkout shows 41.96 for the same cart.

expectation.statement: Every screen shows the cart total that cartTotal computes for the same cart.

claimed_root_cause: CartDrawer rounds the promotion per line through applyPromo, while checkout rounds once per order in cartTotal; which rounding the store intends is not written down.

trace.description: Sums line totals after a per-line promotion.
Rounds each discounted line to cents.

evidence.description: Drawer total 41.97 and checkout total 41.96 for the same cart.

blockers: Consult dlg-01 ended judged_neither: the opus judge panel found that neither the hunter nor the peer showed which rounding rule the store intends.
The fable tier that the judge route asks for is declared unavailable for this owner, so no stronger model could settle it.

validation_plan.owner: Confirm whether promotions round per line or per order, or rerun this consult when the fable tier is available.
validation_plan.local: Add the intended rule to CONTRIBUTING.md as a project rule; a later run then confirms or rejects the record.

stronger_model_needed.reason: The decision depends on reading three modules for an unwritten business rule; the available opus judges agreed that the evidence does not settle it.

deliberation.summary: h2-cart asked whether the drawer figure is stale state or a different rounding rule. Peer q1-cart-state (resilience lens) found no stale state and said the difference is a rounding choice. h2-cart kept its position; the judge panel ruled neither.
The fable judge was replaced by two independent opus judges at xhigh effort; both ruled neither, so no deciding judge was needed.
Phase 5 record verification ran as two opus verifiers in place of fable; both kept the record as needs_validation.

title: A second tap on Place order creates a second order on a slow connection
description: On a phone with a slow 4G profile, two taps on Place order about 50 ms apart create two orders and two card charges in the disposable data.

expectation.statement: One activation of Place order creates exactly one order.

root_cause: PlaceOrderButton stays enabled while the request is pending and the orders endpoint accepts the same cart twice because it has no idempotency key.

trace.description: Calls placeOrder without disabling the button or tracking a pending request.
Posts the cart with no idempotency key.
Inserts an order and charges the card for every request.

evidence.description: Two POST requests 52 ms apart, both 201.
Independent reproduction by a Phase 3 panel verifier: 3 of 3 runs created two orders.

conditions.description: The slow 4G profile keeps the request pending long enough for the second tap.

execution.user_perspective: The customer taps once more because nothing seems to happen, then sees two orders and two charges.
steps: Tap Place order twice about 50 ms apart under slow4g
Count orders with the read-only count command
execution.observed_result: Two orders and two charges in 3 of 3 runs.

remediation.strategy: Disable PlaceOrderButton while the request is pending and send an idempotency key that createOrder deduplicates.
remediation.regression_check: A test that calls placeOrder twice with the same key and expects one order; a probe double-tap check under slow4g.

impact.reason: A customer is charged twice; support must refund by hand.

reach.reason: Customers on slow connections who tap again while the request is pending.

confidence.reason: Reproduced by the hunter and independently by both Phase 3 panel verifiers, 3 of 3 runs each.

deliberation.summary: Strong candidate verification is routed to fable, which is declared unavailable; two independent opus verifiers at xhigh effort both reproduced the duplicate order and agreed on confirmed.
Phase 5 record verification ran as two opus verifiers in place of fable; both confirmed the record without changes.
